todo_line: - [ ] 004 Render only a validated expected-club-origin `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` body URL as an escaped primary action in member-message HTML, retain the URL in text email, and focused-test safe and unsafe rendering without introducing arbitrary HTML or subject-based authorship.
outcome: Render the fixed request body's validated current-club targeted-add URL as an escaped `Add Eve to Board` primary action in root member-message HTML while preserving the exact plain-text body and safe ordinary-message behavior.
scope: Extend root member-message HTML presentation to recognise the stored body's add-action line and URL, validate the URL against the request's current club origin and exact `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` route shape, and render the action with `EmailTemplates.primary_action/3`.
Keep all body prose as escaped plain-text-derived HTML; only the validated action line/URL may become trusted component markup, and the helper must escape both the derived button label and URL.

Add focused `MemberMessageEmail` tests proving the expected current-club URL becomes an `Add Eve to Board` action, root text email remains byte-for-byte the stored body, unrelated subject text cannot trigger an action, and malformed or unsafe origin/route candidates remain escaped non-action text.
scope_exclusions: Do not change `RequestGroupAccess`, its accepted server-owned subject/body/recipient construction, message events, delivery dispatch, provider behavior, or the general web composition policy.
Do not add an HTML body to the domain model, action metadata, a request entity/status, arbitrary rich text, general URL linkification, or a subject-line marker for trusted/system messages.

Do not implement the Request access placeholder, sending/sent feedback, targeted-add route, explicit addition, welcome flow, browser journey, or placeholder assertion updates; those remain tasks 005 through 008.
Do not edit acceptance feature files, step definitions, application UI, routes, iteration planning documents, ADRs, or planner-owned delivery artifacts.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command in this packet.

references.facts: Root text output currently returns `request.body` unchanged. Root HTML sends the whole body through `EmailTemplates.plaintext_to_html/2`; keep that escaping baseline and introduce only a narrowly validated component action.
`plaintext_to_html/2` escapes body text and `primary_action/3` already escapes its label and URL while rendering the approved table-backed button plus printed fallback URL.
The renderer receives the stored `body` and authoritative projected `club_slug`; no new action metadata is required.

`url/2` builds the configured scheme, host, and port for the specific club slug. `safe_club_url?/1` accepts any configured club subdomain, so it is not sufficient by itself for the required expected-current-club-origin check.

The accepted body format contains `Add <person name> to <group name>:` immediately followed by the server-generated current-club `/groups/<group id>/members/add/<person id>` URL; preserve this producer unchanged.
Use the existing typed-ID contract when validating the route's group and person path segments rather than accepting arbitrary non-empty segments.
This is the focused renderer test seam and already builds requests with controllable club slug, subject, and body.
Accepted coverage fixes the exact stored body and ClubSite-generated target URL; task 004 consumes that representation and must not revise its semantics.

Email link presentation requires validation of the management URL itself, not the subject or prose; surrounding text and label remain escaped, and ordinary links to the same safe destination may receive the same presentation.
The approved email state shows `Add Eve to Board` as the primary action with a printed fallback URL and explains that opening it only reaches later read-only route behavior.

constraints: Treat the entire member-authored body as untrusted. Parse only enough structure to identify an unambiguous action-label line immediately associated with its candidate URL, and pass the label and URL through existing escaping helpers.

A valid candidate must have the exact configured origin for `request.club_slug` (scheme, host, and effective port), no userinfo, query, or fragment, and exactly `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` with valid typed group and person IDs. A sibling club host, lookalike host, root Memba host, scheme/port mismatch, extra or missing path segment, wrong ID type, encoded route confusion, or relative/external URL must not become an action.

Do not infer trust from `Access request:` or any other subject. Prove both directions: matching subject without a valid URL produces no action, while a valid same-club route in the supported body shape does not require a magic subject.
For rejected candidates, render the original material only through escaped plaintext HTML and do not emit an `href` or primary-action markup for that candidate.
Keep root `text_body/1` exactly equal to `request.body`, including the URL. Preserve existing root/reply headers, body copy, reply hints, footers, and ordinary bodies without a matching action.
Use existing `MembaWeb.ClubSite`, `Memba.ID`, and `Memba.EmailTemplates` behavior; do not duplicate club-host configuration or hand-roll ID syntax.
Do not use `Process.sleep/1`; keep the focused renderer tests pure and deterministic.
completion_evidence_required: Return every changed path and identify the renderer boundary where validation occurs.

Show that a supported body with the current club's typed targeted-add URL produces escaped `Add Eve to Board` primary-action markup and a printed fallback URL, while `text_body/1` remains exactly the stored body.

List the unsafe cases covered, including at least sibling/lookalike or external origin, malformed/wrong route or typed IDs, injected label/body HTML, and subject-only spoofing; confirm rejected candidates have no action href and remain escaped text.
Confirm ordinary root/reply member-message rendering and the accepted `RequestGroupAccess` body producer were not changed.
Record the focused validation command, working directory, exit status, and test/failure counts; list any unresolved issue.
